title: Information for the Riverside Lantern Walk
transcript:
Good evening, and thank you for helping with the riverside lantern walk. This is our first year using both banks of the river, so even returning volunteers should listen carefully to the route information. The event is intended to be a gentle community walk, not a race, and people may take as long as they need.

Families will collect their lanterns from the pavilion beside the sports field. Each lantern contains a battery light. We are not allowing candles, including those inside glass holders, because the paths can become crowded and children often carry the lanterns close to their clothing.

After collection, visitors follow the blue signs towards the bridge. The red signs lead to the car park and should only be used at the end of the evening. Please do not send families across the grass to save time. Recent rain has made it soft, and the ground is uneven beneath the leaves.

The first stopping point is the bandstand, where a small group will play acoustic music. They will repeat the programme several times, so there is no need for everyone to arrive together. If a crowd begins to block the path, encourage people to move into the open area beside the seating.

Lost property should be taken to the tent near the bridge. A separate team there will also deal with children who have become separated from their families. Volunteers should stay with a child and contact that team rather than trying to search the whole route themselves.

Halfway around the walk, visitors can buy hot drinks. The stall accepts cards, but mobile reception is unreliable, so carrying some cash is sensible. Drinking water is available without charge at two refill points. Please tell visitors that the cups sold at the stall can be reused throughout the evening.

The final section passes close to houses. We have asked the musicians to stop before that section, and we would appreciate your help in keeping voices low. Several residents have young children, and their cooperation has made the new route possible.

If strong winds develop, the organiser may close the bridge and shorten the walk. That decision will be sent to your radios. Do not rely on messages passed along by visitors. Until you receive a direct instruction, keep people moving along the planned route and report any fallen branches to the control team. We will now check that every volunteer's radio is working.

To save batteries in the sound equipment

By following a change in sign colour
